To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) nicotine decreased demand for food, but did not affect essential value, and (2) essential value was equivalent across food magnitudes during the fixed-ratio open economy, but decreased slightly across magnitudes during a closed economy.
(1) the essential value of the food reinforcer was not altered across a range of magnitudes of food reinforcers, and (2) nicotine decreased demand, but did not change the essential value of sucrose.
(a) nicotine decreased demand for food, but (b) the rate of change (elasticity) in demand was unaffected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of nicotine and other drugs of abuse on the demand for natural rewards.
the development and application of behavioral economic models of drug self-administration.
understanding the behavioral mechanisms of drug effects on the essential value and the rate of consumption of food.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present experiments provide evidence that nicotine does not affect the essential value of sucrose, but does affect the rate of demand.
the essential value of nicotine is lower than that of food, but that it is not lower than that of the most preferred food.
the exponential model is an adequate tool for quantifying elasticity and that nicotine does not alter the essential value of palatable food in rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the essential value of the reinforcer is not changed by nicotine, but nicotine does change the demand for the reinforcer.
the essential value of the reinforcer is not affected by nicotine, whereas nicotine does affect the demand for the reinforcer.
the essential value of the good (food) is not changed by the magnitude of the good (number of food pellets) or by the nicotine administration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of change of elasticity is a sensitive measure of the essential value, and that it is possible to measure the essential value of nicotine and food independently.
the exponential equation provides a useful tool for examining the effects of drugs of abuse on the essential value for food. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the exponential demand equation provides a simple, yet powerful tool for quantifying essential value.
